title: Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc)
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is specified for Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) because its 900+ MPa tensile strength allows thin-wall tube shaping without buckling, critical for lightweight frame and component structures. The alpha-beta microstructure delivers 45% higher specific strength than 4140 chromoly steel, translating directly to gram-level weight savings where it matters. Its high-cycle fatigue endurance limit (>500 MPa @10^7 cycles) matches the pedaling load spectrum of Lightweight ventilated disc brake rotor. This rationale is driven by lightweight ventilated disc brake rotor and service environment demands.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for brake rotor hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g with Class 6g gauge
Go/No-Go ring gauging with Class 6g gauge
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for lightweight ventilated disc application
commonFailures: Bearing race brinelling from over-torque - avoided by torque-limiting press-fit tool with ±2% accuracy — critical for lightweight ventilated disc performance

faq.q: Does Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) require special assembly or anti-seize?
faq.a: Yes. Titanium-to-titanium threaded interfaces on Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) are susceptible to galling (cold welding) during assembly. Application of MoS₂ or copper-based anti-seize compound to all threaded contact surfaces is mandatory. Lubricated installation torque values are typically 15-20% lower than dry values. Thread engagement should not exceed 3× thread diameter.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) orders?
faq.a: Standard lead time for Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) is 15-25 business days depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders (3-5 working days) are available for prototype evaluation. Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc)?
faq.a: Each Titanium Brake Rotor (Disc) shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for lightweight ventilated disc.
